title: dedicated: autoscaling burst controls + fleet utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers on Dedicated wanted stronger burst controls and clearer fleet utilization reporting to meet SLA guarantees and avoid noisy autoscale oscillation. This PR adds a configurable burst token bucket for Dedicated autoscalers, exposes per-fleet and per-pool utilization metrics used by the console, and wires those metrics into the autoscaler decision logic to reduce scale churn.

What changed (high level): added a burst controller implementation (token-bucket) that sits in front of scale-up decisions; extended the AutoscalerPolicy proto with burst_* fields; added a utilization summarizer that computes short/long-window duty cycles and tail latency-based load factors; exported new metrics (dedicated_pool_burst_tokens, dedicated_pool_utilization_short, dedicated_pool_utilization_long, dedicated_pool_tail_load_factor) and dashboard templates; updated the Dedicated API to return current burst state for observability; added unit and integration tests; docs and upgrade notes.

Checklist: [x] implement burst token bucket and integrate with controller; [x] add metrics and dashboard panels; [x] add API surface to fetch burst state; [x] tests (unit + e2e); [x] docs + upgrade notes; [ ] schedule canary rollout (follow-up ops task).

Compatibility & rollout: new AutoscalerPolicy fields are backwards compatible (default behavior unchanged). When enabled, the burst controller will cap immediate scale-ups to the configured burst capacity and refill rate. We recommend gradual rollout (canary on 1-2 fleets) and monitoring of dedicated_pool_utilization_short.

Related: ENG-4278 (autoscale stability), ENG-4310 (observability for Dedicated), SUP-987 (customer request from enterprise account).

release_notes: Added configurable burst controls to Dedicated autoscaler (token-bucket) and new utilization metrics + dashboard panels. AutoscalerPolicy gains optional burst fields. Backwards-compatible defaults preserve existing behavior. Operators should review docs and consider a canary rollout.
upgrade_instructions: 1) operators: review docs/ops/dedicated-autoscale.md for new AutoscalerPolicy fields and defaults. 2) apply updated autoscaler-configmap patch in a canary fleet. 3) monitor dedicated_pool_utilization_short and dedicated_pool_burst_tokens for the first 24-72h. 4) rollback instructions included in docs if unexpected throttling observed.
notes_for_ops: This change reduces immediate scale-up spikes by capping burst capacity. Expect fewer transient overprovision events and reduced scale oscillation. If customers report perceived slower scale-ups, check burst refill rate and consider increasing burst_capacity for the affected fleet.
